description: The line plot illustrates the performance of two large vision-language models—GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet—on a reasoning task measured by Accuracy@1 (%) as a function of the number of child nodes (tree width) in a multimodal tree search, ranging from 1 to 7. The x-axis, labeled “Num. of Child Nodes (Tree Width),” is linear and spans integer values 1, 3, 5, and 7. The y-axis, labeled “Accuracy@1 (%)”, is also linear, ranging from 15 to 35 with major tick marks at intervals of 5. The GPT-4o model, represented by a solid blue line with circular markers, starts at 24.4% accuracy at tree width 1, rises to 28.9% at width 3, peaks at 34.4% at width 5, and then declines to 31.1% at width 7. The Claude-3.5-Sonnet model, shown as a solid light blue line with ‘x’ markers, begins at 26.7% at width 1, slightly increases to 27.8% at width 3, then steadily decreases to 24.4% at width 5 and further drops to 20.0% at width 7. The plot visually demonstrates that GPT-4o benefits more from increased tree width up to 5, while Claude-3.5-Sonnet’s performance degrades beyond width 3.
